transcript_whisper.text: 18th May 1974, وہ دن تھا جب بھارت بھی اٹیومک پاولٹ کنتریس کے قطار میں آکھڑا ہوا اب ہمیں نہ تو چینا کر در تھا اور نہ ہی انتناشل سکڑٹی کمیٹیس کی آگے سورکشہ کے لئے ہاتھ پھلانے کی ضرورت اوری دنیا جہاں سوچ رہی تھے کی انڈیا صرف نون الائن رہکر اپنے اینڈ نیٹس کو بھی پورا کر پائیگی یا نہیں وہی ہمارے دیش میں ایک بار نہیں بلکی دو دو بار پر مانو ٹیسٹنک ہوا۔ 1974 میں جب انڈرا گاندی کی آدیش پر فیزیست راجہ رمانانے پوکھرڈ میں پہلی اٹیومک ٹیسٹ کیا تو پورے بیشڈوں

first_sentence.english: 18 May 1974 — the day India joined the queue of atomic-powered countries…

shots: Title card: 18'TH MAY 1974 over desert ground
Archival B&W figures walking in desert

on_screen.note: Date card + archival montage + world reaction + the blast: the whole story in 30 s.

opening_type.sentence_devanagari: 18 मई 1974… वह दिन था जब भारत भी एटॉमिक पावर्ड कंट्रीज़ की कतार में खड़ा हो गया…
opening_type.english: 18 May 1974 — the day India joined the queue of atomic-powered countries…
opening_type.why: Date first, then the change it caused. Same shape as the 1971 hook.

findings: No hook opens with a question: 6/6 are declarative statements.
4/6 open with a date or year in the first spoken line; 1 more opens with a place ('55 miles west of Mexico City'); only the biography opens with a riddle.
The event films (26/11, 1993) both add the same clause: 'an ordinary day... unaware of tomorrow'.
Nobody appears on camera: the first frame is always a place (street, map, prison, desert).
Cutting inside the hook is bimodal too: 3-5 shots for place/slow hooks, 10-13 for event montage hooks.
The hook visual and the hook line are redundant on purpose: the map/date on screen repeats what the voice says.

master_hook_formula.name: Date -> Ordinary World -> Foreshadow -> Evidence
master_hook_formula.one_liner: Open on a place and a date, describe the world in one calm sentence, add a foreshadow clause, then cut to proof — never ask a question, never show a face.

beats.name: Date or place stamp
beats.voice: first 4-6 words are the date/year, or a place with a superlative
beats.screen: establishing shot of the place; on-screen date if the date is spoken
beats.evidence: 4/6 date + 1/6 place ('55 miles west of Mexico City')

beats.name: Ordinary world
beats.voice: one sentence of 'life as usual' — traffic, morning, the city at work
beats.screen: street / crowd / transit footage, no faces introduced
beats.evidence: 26/11 and 1993 use the exact 'ordinary day, unaware of tomorrow' clause

beats.name: Foreshadow
beats.voice: 'unaware of its own tomorrow' / 'under the shine, a dark shadow' / 'the toughest prison'
beats.screen: the fourth shot turns: money, a silhouette, a guard tower, a blast cloud

beats.name: Evidence cut
beats.voice: the narrator states the event; the voice keeps running
beats.screen: first news card or archive insert lands here (26/11: 18 s, 1993: 11.8 s newspapers)
beats.evidence: news cards inside 30 s in 2/6; archive inside 30 s in 4/6

card_rules: No question in the first line, ever.
Date first, story second: the number is the promise.
One calm sentence before the turn; the contrast does the work.
Never open on a face or a title card: open on a place.
Repeat the hook fact on screen (date card, map, sign) so the eye and ear agree.
3-5 shots if the hook is a place; 10-13 if it is an event montage.
master_hook_formula.template_devanagari: [तारीख/साल] की [सुबह/शाम], [जगह] में [आम दिन वाली एक बात]… सब कुछ सामान्य था, [कल से अनजान / किसी को अंदाज़ा नहीं था]… और फिर [वो घटना जो सब बदल देगी].
master_hook_formula.template_english: On [date], in [place], [one sentence of ordinary life]… everything looked normal, unaware of what was coming… and then [the event that changed everything].
master_hook_formula.performance_note: All six hooks are self-contained: a viewer can retell the premise after 30 s without any context, and the film still has a promise (what happened next) left to pay off.
